facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Legend has it that the Pandavas originally constructed the Kedarnath shrine to atone for sins committed during the Mahabharata war.
facts.text: According to Garhwal folklore, the Pandava brothers erected the earliest Kedarnath shrine to expiate the guilt of Gotra Hatya incurred during the Kurukshetra battle before making their journey toward Swargarohini.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Using the size of the lichen and some statistical refinements... Kedarnath temple survived being buried under the snow for almost 400 years.
facts.text: A lichenometric moraine study published in Current Science by Dr. R. K. Chaujar indicated that the Chorabari glacier advanced during the Little Ice Age, keeping the Kedarnath temple buried under snow and ice for nearly 400 years between 1300 and 1900 CE.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: According to scientists of Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology, Dehradun, Kedarnath temple survived being buried under the snow for almost 400 years... the temple structure has several yellow lines, which were formed as the glacier slowly moved over the stones.
facts.text: Scientists from the Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology identified yellowish striation marks and polish tracks across the temple's outer granite surfaces, caused by the gradual movement of glacial ice and embedded debris over several centuries.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Chaujar's own paper lays out three separate possibilities and does not pick one: the temple was built before any glacier reached that spot, the temple was built after the ice had already advanced and then receded, or the temple was somehow constructed through or around an existing glacier.
facts.text: Scientists dispute whether the Kedarnath shrine was literally entombed beneath a moving glacier during the Little Ice Age or if advancing lateral moraines simply flanked the perimeter while snow accumulation enveloped the roofline.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The interlocked stones with iron clamps without the use of mortar or cement allowed the structure to withstand extreme pressures.
facts.text: Field documentation by the Archaeological Survey of India verified that Kedarnath temple was erected without mortar using dry ashlar masonry with interlocking stone joints and iron dowels, granting it high resistance to seismic energy and water loads.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: It recorded 210 mm of rain in 12 hours another 115 fell in the next 12 hours that is 325 mm in a single day.
facts.text: Meteorological records from the Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology camp documented that 325 millimetres of rainfall fell over the Chorabari glacial catchment within twenty-four hours immediately preceding the flash flood.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The bursting of this lake led to its complete draining within 5–10 min as reported by the watch and ward staff of the Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology.
facts.source_name: Current Science / Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology
facts.text: The moraine-dammed Chorabari Lake, located approximately two kilometres north of the temple, collapsed its natural terminal wall on the morning of June 17, 2013, draining its entire volume in less than ten minutes.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: A massive boulder got lodged roughly thirty feet behind the rear wall of the temple during the flash flood.
facts.text: A massive erratic boulder washed down by the Chorabari debris surge came to a halt roughly nine metres behind the north-facing rear wall of the Kedarnath sanctum.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The boulder split the water and rubble in two directions and sent it around the structure instead of through it.
facts.text: Post-flood geotechnical analysis established that the giant boulder acted as an emergency hydro-barrier, bifurcating the incoming torrent and debris flow around both flanks of the monument rather than ramming its rear masonry.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Devotees began worshipping the protective rock behind the shrine as Bhim Shila, honoring the legend of Bhima guarding the temple.
facts.text: Local priests and devotees named the protective boulder 'Bhim Shila', in the belief that the Pandava warrior Bhima placed the rock to shield Lord Shiva's holy seat from devastation.

intro.prompt: 16:9 landscape, 1920x1080, about 8 seconds, photorealistic and cinematic, bright vivid colour. Setting: dramatic wide view of an ancient grey stone Himalayan temple half buried in a towering wall of blue-white glacial ice under a stormy sky, snow peaks behind, wind-blown snow, the lower fifth smooth untouched snow. The background is real and in motion behind him (as fits the place: waves, mist, leaves, flags, lamps flickering, people walking, traffic, light shifting); never a still, flat or heavily blurred backdrop. If the scene shows the past, it is ancient India: Indian people in dhotis, sarees and angavastram, warriors with bows, spears and bronze or leather armour, carved stone pillars, oil lamps; never European knights, plate armour, castles or anything medieval European. Movement and framing: like a TV news reporter on location, he walks toward the camera while he speaks: he starts three or four steps back, seen from the knees up, walks steadily and confidently toward the lens, and stops at a medium shot from the waist up for the last words. His whole head and both shoulders stay inside the frame the whole time, with clear space above his hair and on both sides; do not crop the top of his head. Lighting: warm key light on the face, a soft rim light on the hair, matched to the scene; flattering, no harsh shadows, no dull or flat grey look. SG [locked] walking tall and lively, shoulders open, energetic and confident, wearing a rust-orange kurta with a cream stole. Speaks from the first frame, mouth matched to the words, steady eye contact with the lens. Face and delivery: an excited, high-energy presenter breaking a big story, full of life, as if he cannot wait to tell you. Bright, wide-awake eyes, lively eyebrows that lift on the question, a big, bright, genuine smile. On the question his voice rises with excitement as he strides closer. On the last line a big confident smile, a quick nod and a point at the viewer. Natural blinking, lively head movement. Never sad, gloomy, worried, tired, sleepy, flat or bored; never a frown, never a blank face. Voice: energetic, upbeat, punchy and clear, a brisk pace, rising on the question, with a quick beat before the last line. Hands: energetic, natural gestures at chest height: a quick point toward the scene behind him on the question and an open palm toward the viewer on the last line; never limp, never hanging still by his sides. Camera: eye level, steady, holding its place as he walks up to it (a very slight slow push-in at most), slight handheld feel. Empty hands, no prop. @SGMythWorld watermark in the top right corner, white, bold, 80% opacity. No captions, no subtitles, no other on-screen text. No hologram, no floating screen, no graph, no chart, no laptop, tablet, monitor, TV or glowing blue panel anywhere in the frame. Export at 1920x1080.
